# The show {background-color="#00001a"}

::: {.notes}
About 10 minutes.
:::

## Commands to go on air {.commands}

```{.bash code-line-numbers="7-8,19-20,22-23"}
# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/alfre2v/zombie-radio && cd zombie-radio

# Install the tooling, Ansible included (once per clone)
make install && make ans-deps

# Wire AI box IP in Ansible hosts.yml
make ans-set ENV=cloud IP=<box-address>

# Deploy the AI components (run only once)
make ans-deploy ENV=cloud

# Install client (TalkWithZombies) on laptop, with stand-in voices
make client-mac
# The real cast: download the EARS human voices, then copy them into the client
python3 tools/voices/fetch_ears.py --speakers 7,17,26,63 --types 'emo_*_sentences' --fetch
uv run python tools/voices/cast_voices.py --all-emotions

# Open SSH tunnel to AI box
make ssh-tunnel ENV=cloud

# Serve app on laptop (127.0.0.1 by default)
cd ~/TalkWithZombies-client && .venv/bin/uvicorn app.main:app --port 8000
```

::: {.notes}
Everything on this slide is done before the talk, not live: the clone, the wiring, the deploy (once, about 7 minutes
on a fresh VM), the client's install, the tunnel and the app. On stage, only explain what each line does.

NOT ON THE SLIDE, BUT NEEDED ONCE PER CLONE — make install (the Python tooling, Ansible included, into .venv with uv)
and make ans-deps (the pinned Ansible collections, kept inside the project). Every make target runs Ansible through
uv run, so nothing is installed system-wide. make help lists every target.

BEFORE THE FIRST COMMAND, ON HYPERSTACK'S CONSOLE (every new VM) — attach a public IP (a new VM has none), enable SSH
access (the firewall denies everything by default), optionally enable ICMP so it answers ping. The SSH identity is
declared once in the inventory: user ubuntu, key ~/.ssh/hyperstack_2026.

LINE BY LINE
- ans-set ENV=cloud IP=… writes the box's address into deploy/ansible/inventories/cloud/hosts.yml, replacing the
  REPLACE_ME placeholder; it refuses if the file is already wired. A git hook blocks any commit of a wired file
  (the never-commit hook): addresses never reach the public repo. make ans-unset ENV=cloud restores the placeholder when the box
  is gone.
- ans-deploy ENV=cloud runs site.yml against the box. Idempotent: from zero or from any half-done state, it converges;
  a healthy box reports changed=0 (in about 30 seconds). The first deploy downloads about 11 GB of models: about 7
  minutes once apt has finished on a fresh VM, budget 15. Each run is logged on the laptop in
  ~/.config/zombie-radio/logs/; ANS_VERBOSE=1 adds detail; ANS_ARGS passes extra options (ANS_ARGS=-K asks a sudo
  password, for a home PC). make ans-check-syntax ENV=cloud parses the playbook without touching a box.
- client-mac checks it is on a Mac with git, python3, say and afconvert (it installs none), clones the fork at its
  pinned tag, makes the virtual environment, seeds settings.yaml with the tunnel's ports, and creates four placeholder
  personas with voices made by macOS's say. A locally modified clone fails loudly instead of being overwritten. The
  real cast — EARS recordings, one per mood — is two more lines: fetch_ears.py downloads the four speakers' clips
  (p007 Daniel, p017 Ralph, p026 Moira, p063 Samantha; about 23 emotions each) into zombie-radio-datasets/ears/,
  outside git, because EARS is CC BY-NC; cast_voices.py then copies them into ~/TalkWithZombies-client/Personas/ as
  ref.wav and ref-<emotion>.wav, evened out in loudness. Who voices whom: tools/voices/cast.yaml; which recording each
  mood uses: the story's overtones.yaml (docs/runbooks/cast-voices.md).
- ssh-tunnel ENV=cloud reads the address from hosts.yml; it stays in the foreground (its own terminal tab; Ctrl-C
  closes it). One tunnel at a time: the cloud's and the home PC's use the same local ports. Then make check: three ok
  lines (llama, tts, whisper).
- The app serves on 127.0.0.1:8000; open http://localhost:8000/show and pick a look.

IF SOMETHING IS OFF
- After a VM reboot: do nothing — the containers and the voice's service rise by themselves in under a minute; reopen
  the tunnel and run make check. llama.cpp needs up to about 90 s to load the model after a cold start: wait for
  "model loaded" in docker logs llama before diagnosing.
- A fresh, drifted or restored box: make ans-deploy again. Destroying the box and deploying a new one is also fine:
  one command, about 15 minutes.
- Status, logs, the GPU, the health checks: docs/runbooks/box-inspection.md.
:::
